newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates fall on central bank injections.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates fall on central bank injections.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates fell at mid-session on Tuesday, reflecting repeated central bank fund injections to satisfy liquidity demand in the final days before the lunar new year, an annual demand peak, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate had eased by midday to 5.990 percent from Monday's 6.752 close, with 30-day commercial paper falling to 6.00-6.25 percent from 6.25-6.50.

The rates recently have been at traditional annual high levels due to businesses' funding needs ahead of the five-day Chinese new year holiday, which this year starts on February 6 for Taiwan's money markets, dealers said.
The holiday is when successful companies reward employees with cash bonuses, sending short-term money demand spiking.
Rates were expected to fall sharply after the holiday.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0840 percent against 6.0815.
